name: Nick DiCeglie
pollingDetails: No public poll found. SD 18 voted R+9.6 for president in 2024 and Republicans hold a double-digit voter-registration edge (per Florida Politics, Oct 2026). DiCeglie won the open seat with 56.9% in 2022 and is a heavy favorite against an under-funded challenger.
raised: ~$208k campaign + ~$2M in Friends of Nick DiCeglie PC (multi-cycle); ~$600k PC + ~$76k campaign cash on hand (Florida Politics, reports through Aug 13 2026)
backers: Friends of Nick DiCeglie political committee, Florida Chamber of Commerce, Pinellas Sheriff Bob Gualtieri, business and industry donors
lgbtqDetails: Voted YES on HB 1557 (Parental Rights in Education, the so-called Don't Say Gay law) as a House member on Feb 24, 2022, and YES on SB 254 (ban on gender-affirming care for minors) in the Senate on May 4, 2023, per official roll calls.
platform: Former owner of a family sanitation business; served in the Florida House 2018-2022 before winning SD 18 in 2022. Chairs the Senate Appropriations Committee on Transportation, Tourism and Economic Development. Sponsored SB 180 (2025 hurricane-recovery law) and its 2026 fix SB 840, plus a bill to eliminate documentary stamp taxes for first-time homebuyers; campaigns on affordability, storm recovery and government efficiency.
controversy: SB 180, which he sponsored in 2025, barred local governments from tightening land-use rules after hurricanes and drew more than two dozen lawsuits from cities and counties; he conceded 'unintended consequences' and pushed a narrowing fix in 2026 (Fox 13, Florida Politics, The Invading Sea). In 2023 the Tampa Bay Times and Florida Phoenix reported his family business partners sued him alleging he embezzled company money before taking office; DiCeglie disputed the claims.
endorsements: Florida Chamber of Commerce (June 2026), Pinellas Sheriff Bob Gualtieri (Aug 2026)

name: Karla Kemp
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Kemp won the Aug 18 Democratic primary with 59.9% but faces an R+9.6 district (2024 presidential vote) and an incumbent with roughly 500 times her cash; Florida Politics (Oct 2026) called the seat one a 'blue wave' would likely skip.
raised: ~$1,330 raised / ~$3,100 spent in state account (Florida Politics, report through July 31 2026); her earlier federal CD 13 committee reported $10,639 receipts (FEC)
backers: Small individual donors; no major PAC support reported
lgbtqDetails: No votes or specific public statements on LGBTQ+ issues found; she is not on Equality Florida PAC's Oct 16, 2026 endorsement list, though she runs as a self-described progressive.
platform: Former paramedic and firefighter turned insurance agent and sustainability consultant with degrees in business management and sustainability. Started 2026 in the CD 13 congressional race, then switched to SD 18 in June after Leela Gray entered. Runs on health care access, property insurance and coastal resilience, election protections, government accountability and taking on corporate monopolies to lower costs.
controversy: Florida Politics (Oct 2026) reported she avoids the 'socialist' label publicly while privately describing herself as a 'hardcore Bernie and AOC fan' and 'most definitely a Progressive,' and that her campaign had spent more than it raised.
endorsements: Pinellas County Democratic Party slate, Creative Loafing Tampa Bay
primaryResult: won Aug 18 Democratic primary 59.9%-40.1% over Linda Kellis Harris (21,442 to 14,385 votes)

name: Chris Nocco
pollingDetails: No public poll found. This is a special election to finish retiring Sen. Ed Hooper's term (winner must run again in 2028). Hooper won the Pasco/Pinellas district with 61.7% in 2024, and Nocco, a four-term sheriff with the entire GOP establishment behind him, is a heavy favorite over a first-time candidate with under $10k.
raised: $820,764 raised / $309,707 spent across campaign and committee (Transparency USA aggregate, report date not shown); news reports put his campaign account above $230k as of late Aug 2026
backers: Friends of Chris Nocco political committee, Florida Republican Senatorial Campaign Committee, Florida Chamber of Commerce, Florida Medical Association PAC, development and real-estate donors (incl. a $10k gift reported by Jason Garcia's Seeking Rents, Oct 2026)
lgbtqDetails: No legislative votes and no specific public statements on LGBTQ+ issues found; he is endorsed by Gov. DeSantis and AG Uthmeier, who have championed the state's culture-war agenda.
platform: Pasco County Sheriff since Gov. Rick Scott appointed him in 2011; re-elected unopposed in 2016, 2020 and 2024 and resigning in November to take the seat. Former deputy chief of staff to House Speaker Marco Rubio; served on President Trump's Homeland Security Advisory Council. Campaign is built on public safety, 'protecting families and defending freedom' and his law-enforcement record; few specific policy positions published.
controversy: The Tampa Bay Times' Pulitzer-winning 2020 'Targeted' series exposed his intelligence-led policing program, which used an algorithm and school records to flag residents and 400-plus schoolchildren for repeated deputy visits; in Dec 2024 the Sheriff's Office settled a federal civil-rights suit, admitting the program violated the First, Fourth and Fourteenth Amendments and agreeing to dismantle it (Florida Phoenix, Fox 13). A Florida appeals court ruled in May 2025 that his office unlawfully withheld records on the at-risk youth list. The Hernando Sun and Pasco Herald also noted he is leaving the sheriff's job mid-term to run.
endorsements: Gov. Ron DeSantis, U.S. Sens. Rick Scott and Ashley Moody, U.S. Reps. Anna Paulina Luna, Laurel Lee and Gus Bilirakis, AG James Uthmeier, CFO Blaise Ingoglia, Ag Commissioner Wilton Simpson, Senate President-designate Jim Boyd, Sens. Jay Trumbull, Danny Burgess and Nick DiCeglie, Pinellas Sheriff Bob Gualtieri, Florida Chamber of Commerce (July 2026), Florida Medical Association PAC, Florida Republican Senatorial Campaign Committee
primaryResult: n/a - no special primary was held; per the Florida Division of Elections (July 8 2026) both party nominees advanced directly to the Nov 3 special general election

name: Jordan Hensley
pollingDetails: No public poll found. First-time candidate with roughly $6,700 against a sheriff who has raised hundreds of thousands in a district Ed Hooper carried with 61.7% in 2024; he entered only because no other Democrat filed.
raised: ~$6,700 in campaign account (Pasco Herald / Tampa Bay 28, Aug 31 2026)
backers: Small individual donors; Pinellas County Democratic Party
lgbtqDetails: No votes or specific public statements on LGBTQ+ issues found; not on Equality Florida PAC's Oct 16, 2026 list.
platform: Bartender at the Fenway Hotel rooftop bar in Dunedin, originally from Northeast Ohio, 13-year district resident with no prior political experience. Says he and his wife live paycheck to paycheck and that voters deserve a non-corporate alternative; campaign centers on cost of living, affordability and public-education funding (Hernando Sun Q&A, Oct 22 2026).
endorsements: Pinellas County Democratic Party, Creative Loafing Tampa Bay, Florida Progressives!, Democratic Environmental Caucus of Florida
primaryResult: n/a - no special primary was held; per the Florida Division of Elections (July 8 2026) both party nominees advanced directly to the Nov 3 special general election

name: Adam C. Anderson
pollingDetails: No public poll found. HD 57 (Palm Harbor/Oldsmar area) voted R+16.6 for president in 2024; Anderson won re-election 58.8%-36.8% over Kelly Johnson in 2024 and is a heavy favorite.
backers: Florida Chamber of Commerce; health-care and business donors (campaign-finance aggregator pages could not be retrieved)
lgbtqDetails: Voted YES on SB 254 (ban on gender-affirming care for minors) on May 4, 2023, per the official House roll call; he was not yet in office for the 2022 HB 1557 vote.
platform: Financial executive (CEO of MRA Capital Partners, FSU real-estate and finance graduate) first elected in 2022. Chairs the House Health Care Facilities & Systems Subcommittee; best known for pediatric rare-disease work after losing his son to Tay-Sachs: the Sunshine Genetics Act newborn genetic-screening pilot, the Florida Institute for Pediatric Rare Diseases at FSU, and adding Duchenne muscular dystrophy to newborn screening.
primaryResult: unopposed in primary (no primary challenger on the Florida Division of Elections candidate list)

name: Wendy Hoy
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Late-entry 'run everywhere' challenger in an R+16.6 district (2024 presidential vote) where the Democrat took under 40% in 2024.
backers: Small individual donors; Pinellas County Democratic Party
lgbtqDetails: No specific LGBTQ+ record found; her platform opposes 'government overreach into private lives' but does not address LGBTQ+ issues, and she is not on Equality Florida PAC's list.
platform: Oldsmar resident and former assisted-living administrator and Head Start director; guardian ad litem volunteer, Kiwanian, library board and foster-care charity board member. Entered in June 2026 after learning Anderson was unopposed. Runs on affordability (property and auto insurance), restoring local control, defending voting rights, supporting public schools and libraries, and regulating data centers.
endorsements: Pinellas County Democratic Party, Creative Loafing Tampa Bay

name: Kimberly "Kim" Berfield
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Rematch of 2024, which Berfield won 57.6%-42.4%; the Clearwater-based district voted R+12.1 for president in 2024 and Republicans outnumber Democrats roughly 38% to 30% of registered voters (Florida Politics).
raised: ~$390,450 in contributions (Transparency USA aggregate for the candidate, date not shown; may include committee and prior-cycle money)
backers: Florida Chamber of Commerce; health-care, hospital and business donors
lgbtqDetails: Voted YES on SB 254 (ban on gender-affirming care for minors) on May 4, 2023, per the official House roll call; she was not in office for the 2022 HB 1557 vote.
platform: Clearwater native who served in the House 2000-2006, lost a 2006 Senate race, was deputy secretary of the Florida Department of Health and a lobbyist for All Children's Hospital, then returned to the House in 2022. 2026 bills include local housing assistance plans (HB 267), paid leave for living organ donors (HB 493), public pool safety (HB 633) and a $16M claims bill for a tourist injured at a faulty Clearwater crosswalk (HB 6513).

name: Bryan Beckman
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Lost the same matchup 42.4%-57.6% in 2024; district voted R+12.1 for president in 2024.
raised: ~$109,079 in contributions for the 2026 race (Transparency USA, date not shown)
backers: Individual donors, Democratic and environmental groups, Equality Florida PAC
lgbtqDetails: Endorsed by Equality Florida PAC (list updated Oct 16, 2026) and the Stonewall Democrats of Pinellas County.
platform: Clearwater Democrat who spent his career with a global food company leading warehouse and transportation teams; founder and president of the Pinellas Green Foundation and Sierra Club Ready for 100 volunteer. Managed his wife Kathleen Beckman's 2024 Clearwater mayoral campaign. Runs on lowering insurance, housing and health-care costs, reproductive rights, teacher pay, flooding and pollution.
endorsements: Equality Florida PAC, Stonewall Democrats of Pinellas, Pinellas County Democratic Party, Creative Loafing Tampa Bay, former Rep. Ben Diamond, former Clearwater Mayor Rita Garvey (40-plus endorsements per Florida Politics)

name: Berny Jacques
pollingDetails: No public poll found. HD 59 (Largo/Seminole) voted R+16.0 for president in 2024; Jacques won 58.7% in 2024 and faces a challenger with no campaign website or reported fundraising.
raised: $85,101 raised / $20,014 spent (Transparency USA candidate page, date not shown; affiliated PC Florida Values Coalition not included)
backers: Florida Values Coalition political committee, Florida Chamber of Commerce, Florida PBA / SunCoast PBA, law-enforcement groups
lgbtqDetails: Voted YES on SB 254 (ban on gender-affirming care for minors) on May 4, 2023, per the official House roll call; not in office for the 2022 HB 1557 vote.
platform: Haitian-born former Pinellas-Pasco assistant state attorney and Big Brothers Big Sisters executive, elected in 2022 after losing a 2018 primary to DiCeglie. Hard-line on immigration: filed bills for mandatory private-employer E-Verify (HB 955, 2025), compensation for victims of crimes by undocumented immigrants (2025) and a presumption of fault for undocumented drivers in crashes (HB 1307, 2026); also pushes property-tax cuts and a bill to bar gaming outside the Seminole compact.
controversy: L'Union Suite and The Floridian reported criticism of his 2026 HB 1307 creating a legal presumption of fault against undocumented drivers; his campaign site touts a claim that Democrats want to 'import the third world' and his accusation that the City of Largo engaged in unlawful electioneering over a property-tax town hall. A 2022 opponent ad attacked his 'leftist day job' at Big Brothers Big Sisters (Florida Politics).
endorsements: Florida Chamber of Commerce (June 2026), Pinellas County Commissioner Brian Scott, Florida Police Benevolent Association / SunCoast PBA, Rep. Doug Bankson

name: Susan Rochelle Leff
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Paper-thin campaign (no website found as of Sept 2026) in an R+16.0 district (2024 presidential vote).
raised: Not found (her abandoned federal CD 13 committee shows no financial summary at the FEC)
lgbtqDetails: No votes, statements or endorsements on LGBTQ+ issues found.
platform: Largo resident who has never held office. Filed for Congress in CD 13 in Oct 2025, then told the FEC in April 2026 she was suspending that run for lack of funding and would seek HD 59 instead. No platform published; Activate Pinellas lists her positions as 'still being gathered' and her only public channel is Instagram (@srleff).
endorsements: Pinellas County Democratic Party, Creative Loafing Tampa Bay

name: Melissa Rutland
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Open seat vacated by Democrat Lindsay Cross; HD 60 (St. Petersburg) voted D+6.7 for president in 2024 and Democrats have won it both times under the current map, but registration is roughly even at 35% each (Florida Politics). Florida Politics calls it one of Tampa Bay's toughest legislative battles; Rutland leads on money.
raised: ~$103k campaign + $17.5k Friends of Melissa Rutland PC raised; ~$70k cash on hand combined, plus $45k+ in-kind from GOP committees (Florida Politics / St. Pete Cityverse, reports through Aug 21 2026)
backers: Friends of Melissa Rutland political committee, Republican Party of Florida and House GOP in-kind support, Florida Chamber of Commerce, real-estate and business donors
lgbtqDetails: No votes or public statements on LGBTQ+ issues found; her website and coverage avoid social issues and she pledges that 'solutions aren't partisan.'
platform: Fourth-generation Pinellas native, St. Petersburg commercial real-estate attorney and businesswoman who started at Raymond James; three-term St. Petersburg Development Review Commission member (first woman chair) and DeSantis appointee to the Juvenile Welfare Board. Runs on insurance competition and flood infrastructure, targeted property-tax relief, permitting and housing reform, and banning insider trading by elected officials; models herself on the late Rep. Bill Young.
endorsements: Florida Chamber of Commerce (July 2026), Pinellas Sheriff Bob Gualtieri, U.S. Rep. Gus Bilirakis, Sens. Ed Hooper and Nick DiCeglie, Reps. Linda Chaney, Berny Jacques and Kim Berfield, County Commissioners Dave Eggers, Kathleen Peters and Brian Scott, former St. Petersburg Mayors Rick Baker, Bob Ulrich and Bill Foster

name: Lindsay Polega-Quigley
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Open D+6.7 seat (2024 presidential vote) that Lindsay Cross held by about 7 points in 2024; Polega-Quigley trails Rutland in fundraising but has the retiring incumbent's endorsement and Democratic registration parity.
raised: <$62k campaign + ~$4,750 Leadership, Progress & Quality PC raised; just under $45k cash on hand combined, plus ~$33k in-kind from Democratic committees (Florida Politics / St. Pete Cityverse, reports through Aug 21 2026)
backers: Leadership, Progress & Quality political committee, Florida House Democratic Campaign Committee (in-kind), Ruth's List Florida, Equality Florida PAC, trial-lawyer and individual donors
lgbtqDetails: Endorsed by Equality Florida PAC (list updated Oct 16, 2026) and the Stonewall Democrats of Pinellas County; she also pledges to fight 'culture-war tactics' and did pro bono work representing minors in Florida's judicial-bypass process.
platform: 32-year-old St. Petersburg construction and insurance-litigation attorney (Stetson Law) from a family of public servants. Runs on cost of living: taking on insurers and utility monopolies, ending taxpayer bailouts of insurance companies, housing and health-care costs, water quality and flooding; also supports background checks and safe-storage gun rules, funding public schools and ending 'pay-to-play' politics.
endorsements: Equality Florida PAC, Ruth's List Florida, Stonewall Democrats of Pinellas, Rep. Lindsay Cross, former St. Petersburg Mayor Rick Kriseman, former Rep. Jennifer Webb, Rep. Michele Rayner, Creative Loafing Tampa Bay, Pinellas County Democratic Party

name: Linda Chaney
pollingDetails: No public poll found. HD 61 (St. Pete Beach and the Gulf beaches into south St. Petersburg) voted R+8.5 for president in 2024; Chaney beat Democrat Nathan Bruemmer in 2024 and won 56%-44% in 2022, so she is favored over a first-time grassroots challenger.
raised: $107,618 raised / $23,607 spent (Transparency USA candidate page, date not shown; may include prior cycles)
backers: Florida Chamber of Commerce, business and tourism donors, Foundation for Government Accountability-aligned network (bill drafting, per Orlando Weekly)
lgbtqDetails: Voted YES on HB 1557 (Parental Rights in Education) on Feb 24, 2022 and YES on SB 254 (ban on gender-affirming care for minors) on May 4, 2023, per official House roll calls.
platform: Former St. Pete Beach city commissioner (2007-09) and co-founder of a mobile mammography business sold to AdventHealth; elected to the House in 2020. Vice chair of the Rules Committee and the Infrastructure & Tourism Appropriations Subcommittee. Known for pet-protection bills, beach and infrastructure funding, and sponsoring the 2024 law loosening work-hour limits for 16- and 17-year-olds; voted for the June 2026 special-session HJR 1-F that put Amendment 3 on the ballot.
controversy: Her HB 49 (2024), drafted with the Foundation for Government Accountability, rolled back limits on hours 16- and 17-year-olds can work; it passed the House 80-35 over objections from the Florida Policy Institute and labor groups (Orlando Weekly, CBS Miami, Florida Phoenix). Fox 13 reported her husband William Yovic, who runs a motorcoach company, was charged with stealing state funds after owing more than $100,000 in sales tax; prosecutors dropped the charges in Sept 2026 after he repaid $105,000. Chaney was not accused of wrongdoing and court records say she first flagged the discrepancy.

name: May Thach
pollingDetails: No public poll found. Grassroots first-time candidate in an R+8.5 district (2024 presidential vote) that Chaney has held since 2020; Creative Loafing calls her 'unproven-but-spirited.'
backers: Run for Something PAC, small individual donors; campaign says it uses no establishment political consultants
lgbtqDetails: Endorsed by the Stonewall Democrats of Pinellas County and launched her campaign at Pinellas' Queer Asian Museum (Creative Loafing); not on Equality Florida PAC's Oct 16 list.
platform: Nonprofit professional in the Asian American, Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander (AANHPI) reproductive-justice sector, former teacher and Peace Corps volunteer. Runs on affordability (higher wages, tenant protections, holding property insurers accountable), Medicaid expansion, teacher pay and voucher accountability, flood and storm preparedness, and expanding voter access.
endorsements: Stonewall Democrats of Pinellas, Run for Something, Creative Loafing Tampa Bay, Pinellas County Democratic Party
primaryResult: unopposed in primary (Ballotpedia earlier listed Michael Warner in the Democratic primary, but the Florida Division of Elections candidate list shows only Thach; no primary result reported)
